clue.text: Pay revolutionary involved in armed conflict? Just the opposite

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it
this reverses the stated arrangement, so the conflict goes inside the revolutionary instead of the other way round

blocks.note: a red is a revolutionary leftist
armed conflict between nations

explanation.surface: Paying a rebel who has joined a war, or so it seems until the clue flips itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally the revolutionary sits inside the conflict; the closing phrase swaps outer and inner, a device Everyman likes for a surprise twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a payment given in return for a service, so 'pay' as a noun fits.

clue.text: Teases Spurs?

blocks.note: first meaning: to rib someone is to mock them gently
second meaning: projecting ridges, like spurs of a hill or a leaf's veins

explanation.walkthrough: Spurs suggests Tottenham Hotspur, the London football club nicknamed Spurs; here it is just plural ridges.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is mild mockery; the noun sense is projecting ridges, such as the ridges running off a mountain.

clue.text: What instruments are needed to make a pearly king's suit?

definitions.text: What instruments are needed to make a pearly king's suit?

blocks.clueFragment: What instruments are needed to make a pearly king's suit?
blocks.note: surface reading: which musical instruments go into sewing a Cockney costume
setter's reading: the Cockney rhyming-slang phrase for 'suit' names two instruments

explanation.walkthrough: A pearly king is a Cockney charity figure in a button-covered suit; in Cockney rhyming slang a suit is named by a phrase that rhymes with it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the rhyming-slang term for a suit, built from two wind instruments, and so the Cockney way to say it.

clue.text: Variety of reeds by a mass of water

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so these letters take a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Several kinds of reed growing beside a large body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Sea is a named sea between Africa and Arabia, an example of a great mass of water.

clue.text: Chief wants bit of brisket as well as fillet

indicators.note: only a small piece of the next word is wanted, namely its opening letter

blocks.note: a head is a chief or leader
the opening letter of brisket
'as well as' means in addition

explanation.surface: A head chef wants some brisket along with a fillet steak.
explanation.walkthrough: Brisket and fillet set up a butcher's counter; fillet is really a narrow band worn round the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillet is an old word for a ribbon or band tied round the head, which is what a headband is.

clue.text: Relaxed without difficulty

blocks.note: first meaning: at ease, calm
second meaning: simple to do

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both an untroubled manner, as in 'easy in his mind', and a task that takes no effort.

clue.text: Tyrant in fashion house, without tact possibly

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the letters might be some other arrangement of themselves
'without' in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: Dior is a Paris fashion house
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A despot running a couture house, who perhaps lacks diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without tact' reads as 'tactless', but 'without' means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictator is an absolute ruler, and tyrant is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Dog — curious rare breed I enter

indicators.note: something curious is odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters come out in an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Someone entering an odd rare-breed dog at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aberdeen terrier is another name for the Scottish terrier, a breed of dog.

clue.text: Thirsty boy, one getting drink

blocks.note: dry means thirsty
a boy's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A parched lad going off to fetch himself something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry martini is a cocktail of gin with a little dry vermouth, an example of a drink.

clue.text: In big city, use old flexible financial organisation

indicators.note: something flexible can be bent into a new shape, as these letters are

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Advice to use an old, adaptable firm in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: A building society is a British savings-and-mortgage mutual, much like an American savings and loan.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a member-owned institution that takes savings and lends for home loans, so a kind of financial body.

clue.text: Naturally mean partner

blocks.note: the norm is the mean or average
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: Someone with an unkind spouse, as if it came naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like the adjective for unkind; it is the average.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs mean 'as is usual or to be expected', as in 'naturally, he refused'.

clue.text: Ambassador taken in by Conservative supposition

indicators.note: to be taken in by something is to be held inside it

blocks.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
Tory is the everyday name for a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A diplomat being fooled by a Conservative politician's hunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' reads as deceived, but means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is an idea put forward to explain something, close to an assumption or supposition.

clue.text: Greyish-yellow colour used by artist, a girl

blocks.note: sand is a pale greyish-yellow shade
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter using a pale sandy colour, then a girl appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandra is a female first name, so 'a girl' stands for it in crossword fashion.

clue.text: Pioneer, film pioneer, about to come across with first of rushes

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so one word surrounds another
only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: Charles Pathé was a pioneer of French film and newsreels
to come across something is to find it
the opening letter of rushes

explanation.surface: A pioneering film-maker coming upon the day's rushes, the raw daily footage.
explanation.walkthrough: Rushes are unedited film footage, which fits the cinema scene but only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathfinder is one who finds the way ahead for others, so a trailblazer or pioneer.

clue.text: Northern copper needs to get in fresh bread and tofu

indicators.note: getting in something means going inside it
fresh means new, so the word is made anew in a different order

blocks.note: N abbreviates northern
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman from the North shopping for new bread and tofu.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman but is the metal's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean curd is the literal name for tofu, the soya product, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Top copy, last of six

indicators.note: only the final letter of the next word is wanted

blocks.note: to ape is to imitate
the final letter of six

explanation.surface: A top copy, the last of six made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top copy' sounds like the original of a document; the two words split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or peak of something, its top.

clue.text: Evil-minded man, uncontrollable without one

indicators.note: 'without' here means lacking, so something is removed

blocks.note: a man is a male
violent, out of control
I is the Roman numeral one, removed

explanation.surface: A wicked man who runs wild when left on his own.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolent means wishing harm to others, a synonym of spiteful or evil-minded.

clue.text: Painter from Lyon shivering in Red Square

indicators.note: shivering is trembling about, so the letters are shaken up
one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written
S stands for square, as the first letter of its abbreviation Sq

explanation.surface: An artist from Lyon shivering in Moscow's Red Square.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Square is Moscow's central square, but the two words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Joshua Reynolds was the leading English portrait painter of the 18th century.

clue.text: Deer overcoming broken antler in remote country region

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces that can be reassembled differently
to overcome is to come over, so one piece covers round the other

blocks.note: a hind is a female deer
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A deer that has survived a broken antler, out in the wilds.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinterland is the remote area lying behind a coast or a town, its back country.

clue.text: Shock caused by dangerous feat? No end

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: a stunt is a daring feat

explanation.surface: Alarm caused by a risky feat that seems never to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze or astonish someone, which is to shock them.

clue.text: Obstruct my site conversion

indicators.note: a conversion turns one thing into another, so the letters are remade

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Someone protesting that their building site's redevelopment is being blocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie is to thwart or block someone's progress, hence to obstruct.

clue.text: In cooler temperature delivers baby

blocks.note: taken as written
a fan is a cooling device
T abbreviates temperature

explanation.surface: A mother giving birth when the room is a bit cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler temperature' reads as one phrase; cooler is a noun, the fan.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a very young child, so a baby.

clue.text: Piano, say, in club

blocks.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A piano, for example, in a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' attached to piano; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A putter is the golf club used for short strokes on the green.

clue.text: Petty quarrel caused by difficult son leaving

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so it is dropped from the word

blocks.note: stiff can mean hard or difficult, as in a stiff test
S abbreviates son

explanation.surface: A family squabble sparked by a troublesome son moving out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a slight argument, especially between friends or lovers.

clue.text: Feature of twenty-pence stamp

indicators.note: a feature is a part of something, so the letters are a part of the words

blocks.note: runs across the join of the two halves

explanation.surface: Describing the design on a twenty-pence postage stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: Stamp is not the postal kind: 'of that stamp' means of that kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp in the sense of character or kind is a synonym, as in 'a man of his stamp'.

clue.text: Film nude model by it in ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and remixed

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A film with a nude model posing beside something on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Double Indemnity is Billy Wilder's 1944 film noir about insurance fraud and murder.

clue.text: Effortlessly recites dances associated with Fred initially

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the word's starting letter only

blocks.note: reels are lively Scottish dances
of can mean belonging to or associated with
the opening letter of Fred

explanation.surface: Listing the dances linked with Fred Astaire without a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel off a list is to say it quickly and without effort, as from memory.

clue.text: Tries starter of expensive vehicle

indicators.note: the starter is the first item, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: a judge hears or tries a case
the opening letter of expensive

explanation.surface: Someone test-driving the first of some costly cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Tries suggests attempts; it is the courtroom sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the vehicle that carries a coffin at a funeral.
